text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on June 8th in history:
632 - The Prophet Muhammad, founder of Islam, died.
1042 - Hardicanute, King of England and Denmark, died. He was succeeded in England by Edward the Confessor and in Denmark by Magnus, King of Norway.
1376 - Edward, Prince of Wales, known as the Black Prince, died. He was an outstanding commander during the Hundred Years War.
1810 - Robert Alexander Schumann, German composer best known for his song cycles and piano music, born.
1829 - Sir John Millais, English painter and one of the founders of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood, born.
1845 - Andrew Jackson, American statesman and seventh president 1828-36, died.
1867 - Frank Lloyd Wright, U.S. architect noted for his highly unorthodox approach to building design, born.
1869 - Ives W. McGaffey of Chicago patented his "sweeping machine", the earliest suction type vacuum cleaner.
1876 - George Sand (Armandine-Aurore-Lucile Dupin), French novelist, letter-writer and romantic companion of, among others, the composer Chopin, died.
1915 - William Jennings Bryan, U.S. secretary of state, resigned in disagreement over policy following the German sinking of the Lusitania.
1916 - Professor Sir Francis Crick, British biologist and Nobel Prize winner for determining the molecular structure of DNA, born.
1921 - Suharto, Indonesian President since 1967 and one of the world's longest-serving rulers, born.
1928 - Chiang Kai-shek's nationalist army secured the surrender of Peking after two days.
1929 - Margaret Bondfield became Britain's first woman cabinet minister when she was appointed minister of labour.
1930 - King Carol II returned from exile to resume the throne of Romania.
1942 - Japanese bombers attacked Australia, striking at Sydney and Newcastle.
1947 - Eva Peron, wife of President Juan Peron, was given a tumultuous reception in Madrid by General Franco, a rare greeting by the Spanish dictator for a foreign dignatory.
1965 - U.S. troops were given the authorisation to engage in offensive operations in South Vietnam.
1968 - James Earl Ray, wanted for the assassination of Martin Luther King, was arrested in London.
1968 - Bermuda achieved internal self-government, with a British Governor-General controlling external affairs.
1969 - U.S. President Nixon met the South Vietnamese leader on Midway Island and announced the withdrawal of 25,000 troops.
1969 - Spain closed its border with Gibraltar after Britain refused to hand over the colony.
1969 - Robert Taylor, U.S. film actor in over 70 films including "Camille" and "Ivanhoe", died.
1970 - In Argentina, an army coup unseated President Juan Carlos Ongania.
1973 - Generalissimo Francisco Franco handed over Spain's premiership to Luis Carrero Blanco, after ruling alone for 34 years. He remained as head of state.
1978 - Naomi James sailed into Dartmouth, England, to complete her solo round-the-world voyage, beating Sir Francis Chichester's record by two days.
1982 - In the Falklands War, Argentine planes attacked the landing craft Sir Tristram and Sir Galahad at Bluff Cove, killing 40 men.
1986 - Despite allegations he had been involved in Nazi wartime atrocities, Kurt Waldheim was elected President of Austria.
1993 - Rene Bousquet, the Vichy regime police chief, was shot dead at his Paris home in the Avenue Raphael by a lone gunman.
1995 - Lee Teng Hui became the first Taiwan president to visit the United States, angering Beijing.
1996 - China carried out a nuclear explosion at the Lop Nor test site in northwestern Xinjiang with a blast that rocked the remote region.
